title: Trump Administration Guts Efforts to Prevent Gun Violence, Suppressing Reports
partialText: As the administration works to expand gun rights, hospitals and community groups have lost funding, and reports on preventing firearm injuries have vanished from government websites.

title: Businesses Fear Politicization as Trump Gains More Power Over U.S. Agencies
partialText: A Supreme Court ruling that presidents can fire independent regulators without cause has added volatility for industries that prefer stable enforcement.

title: Trump Promised a Foreign Investment Boom. It’s Getting Harder to Deliver.
partialText: The threat of tariffs may have helped push more capital into the United States, but other factors are pushing it away.

title: After Courting Black Voters, Trump Downplays Black Unemployment
partialText: The president has glossed over persistently high unemployment among African Americans, a group he needed to secure a second term.

title: Democrats Begin to Clash Over Who Replaces Platner Even Before He Exits
partialText: Progressives and moderates are gearing up for a fight over an as-yet-undecided process in Maine to name a Senate nominee to replace Graham Platner after a rape accusation. He still wants a say, too.

title: Trump Expected to Tell Turkey He Is Ready to Restore Access to F-35 Jets
partialText: The president, who is headed to a NATO summit in Ankara this week, had imposed the ban himself amid concerns that giving Turkey the jets could allow Russia to learn about their stealth technology.

title: The Disappearing Las Vegas Buffets Hold a Mirror to the American Soul
partialText: As a once-grand American tradition enters its twilight, our critic journeys to the desert to find out what it all means.

title: Court Upholds Le Pen’s Conviction, but Leaves a Path to Presidency
partialText: An appeals court confirmed Marine Le Pen’s embezzlement conviction, but shortened a ban on her eligibility for elected office. That could let the French far-right leader to run for president in 2027.

title: A Supreme Leader’s Final Crowds
partialText: What you could see when Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s coffin was being driven to a public space in Tehran.

title: Mass Mournings In Qom, Where Khamenei Ruled Supreme Over Iran’s Clerics
partialText: The ceremony for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, held at a site considered sacred by many Shiites, was the latest step in a weeklong funeral organized by Iran’s government.

title: The 39-ish Most Stylish People of 2026, So Far
partialText: On red carpets, on set, onstage and even up in space, they captured our attention with their looks.

title: Caribbean Disparity

title: Louise Lasser, Star of TV’s ‘Mary Hartman,’ Is Dead at 87
partialText: She began her screen career in Woody Allen movies (he was also her husband), but she was best known for her portrayal of the Ohio housewife in the pigtails and puffed sleeves.
